Io is among Jupiter’s four largest moons and was discovered in 1610 by Galileo. Advances in
space exploration and imaging technologies have since enabled scientists to discover even more
moons orbiting Jupiter. For example, scientists used the Voyager 1 space probe to discover
Adrastea in 1979. And more recently, researchers discovered 12 moons using the Dark Energy
Camera at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile. As of 2023, the number of
confirmed moons orbiting Jupiter was 95, and scientists think further exploration will reveal
more.
